RBI closed 66.10 on 09/10 — a new 52-week-high close — and marked a new intraday 52-week high of 66.75, which puts my old 66.30 level 0.67% UNDER structure. That is precisely the AGS.BR mistake: a >= beneath a fresh high is not a breakout order, it is a bid inside the range that fills on nothing. 67.00 clears the 66.75 high by 0.37% and sits 1.36% over the 66.10 close, inside my 2% staleness rule, so it fires only on a genuine breakout close that new data has to produce. The relative strength is the widest on the board and positive on both windows, +32.9pp over 3m and +63.9pp over 6m against VGK, and it earned them the right way: while VGK closed lower four straight sessions from 91.74 to 89.42, RBI closed 65.50, 65.85, 66.10. The volume record behind it is a real breakout, not a candle — 09/08 opened 62.550 and closed AT the 65.50 high, 09/09 followed through on 385,615 shares (1.31x the 294,918 average) with the close at 0.94 of range, and 09/10 extended to a new high on 0.90x. I note the contraction honestly: 0.90x into a new high is attendance, which is why the level goes ABOVE the new high rather than at it — the order now demands the demand I have not yet been shown.
